subject.title: Model configuration accepts unvalidated model names, enabling silent misconfiguration

question: Should unknown configured model refs be warning-only in doctor/config validate, hard validation errors, or left to startup/runtime handling when catalog authority is incomplete?
rationale: The code can enumerate the affected refs, but the product behavior affects custom providers, forward-compatible model names, fail-closed validation, and upgrade safety, so automation should not choose the warning/error semantics alone.

options.title: Warning-first validation
options.body: Add catalog-backed doctor/config warnings for unknown configured refs, clearly distinguishing untrusted/custom catalog absence from likely invalid refs without hard-failing existing setups by default.

options.title: Strict validation
options.body: Reject unknown configured refs at config validation time, accepting a compatibility break unless maintainers also define an explicit escape or migration contract.

options.title: Runtime-only handling
options.body: Keep config validation permissive and rely on startup warmup, runtime errors, and fallback notices rather than adding a new configured-ref analyzer.

recommendation.title: Warning-first validation
recommendation.body: Add catalog-backed doctor/config warnings for unknown configured refs, clearly distinguishing untrusted/custom catalog absence from likely invalid refs without hard-failing existing setups by default.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger has the strongest observed history across the model-selection, config, doctor, and fallback policy surfaces that need the decision.
